definitions.explanation: An organism that lived in a past geological age, now known primarily through fossil remains. Encompasses everything from ancient bacteria to dinosaurs.

examples.japanese: {古生物|こせいぶつ}の{化石|かせき}が{発見|はっけん}された。
examples.english: Fossils of ancient organisms were discovered.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のころから{古生物|こせいぶつ}に{興味|きょうみ}があった。
examples.english: I've been interested in prehistoric life since I was a child.

examples.japanese: この{博物館|はくぶつかん}には{古生物|こせいぶつ}の{標本|ひょうほん}が{数多|かずおお}く{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: This museum has a large number of paleontological specimens on display.

notes:
Combines {古|こ} (ancient) with {生物|せいぶつ} (living thing). Refers to any organism from the geological past, typically studied through fossils.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古生物|こせいぶつ}{学|がく}: paleontology
- {古生物|こせいぶつ}{学者|がくしゃ}: paleontologist
- {古生物|こせいぶつ}の{化石|かせき}: fossils of ancient organisms
- {古生物|こせいぶつ}の{復元|ふくげん}: reconstruction of ancient life forms

RELATED WORDS:
- {化石|かせき}: fossil
- {恐竜|きょうりゅう}: dinosaur
- {絶滅|ぜつめつ}: extinction
- {古生代|こせいだい}: Paleozoic era
